title: US WIC participation, September 2026
question: USDA FNS WIC Program national total participation for September 2026, not seasonally adjusted, first official monthly print, converted to millions of participants.
resolutionSource: USDA Food and Nutrition Service WIC Data Tables
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first USDA FNS WIC Data Tables monthly national print that includes September 2026, using the national Total Participants value for September 2026 in the WIC monthly participation table. Apply the registered transform exactly: multiply the extracted official table value by 0.001 to express the target in millions. Round the resolved millions value to three decimals and ignore later revisions, corrections, annual-summary updates, FRED, and mirrors.
drivers: FY2026 participation was below the FY2025 level after a sharp October-to-February decline
March 2026 showed a partial rebound from February
September is usually at or above spring participation in the same WIC monthly total series
No direct pre-September 2026 policy mechanism was identified that would force a large discontinuity
First-print reporting and state submission timing add material uncertainty

reasoning.text: Release-date basis: the registered target uses resolve-by-bound to 2026-12-30 within the registered 2026-12-22 to 2026-12-30 expected release window for the first official FNS monthly table print covering September 2026.

Base rate/reference class: for a monthly level series, the base rate is same-series persistence plus normal seasonal recovery from spring to late fiscal year. The latest exact FY2026 level I can use is March 2026 at 6.701661 million, after a fall from 6.909938 million in October 2025 and a partial rebound from 6.664580 million in February 2026.

Level, momentum, one-off, and mechanism split: the level is materially below the FY2025 neighborhood near 6.9 million, momentum improved in March after winter attrition, the October-to-February drop may include state reporting or recertification timing as a one-off component, and the policy mechanism does not point to a mechanical September 2026 break before the FY2027 budget year.

Prior/update/interval: model is seasonal persistence from the latest fetched official level. Historical sample uses same-series FY2026 successive changes and 2024 spring-to-September seasonality. Adjustment components: March 2026 level 6.701661 + Mar-to-Sep 2024 seasonal move (6.838250 - 6.680974 = 0.157276) = 6.858937; subtract 0.018937 million for the lower FY2026 level and birth/caseload normalization, giving point 6.840. Interval method uses realized successive monthly changes from fetched WIC history: +0.007963, +0.069415, -0.078428, -0.044612, +0.036426, -0.020183, +0.047568, +0.008453, +0.053049, -0.138204, -0.059123, -0.016311, -0.031720, +0.037081 million; monthly stdev is 0.058156, so six-month horizon sigma = 0.058156*sqrt(6) = 0.142274 million. The 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 1.28*0.142274 = 0.182111 million, so final implied bounds are 6.840 - 0.182 = 6.658 and 6.840 + 0.182 = 7.022 million.

Counter-consideration: upside risk is a stronger summer enrollment rebound, state catch-up reporting, or renewed take-up growth that would land above the interval if the September first print exceeds 7.022 million. Downside risk is persistent FY2026 attrition, funding or administrative disruption, or weaker infant and child caseloads that would land below the interval if the first print is under 6.658 million. Outside the interval would require a larger move than the scaled recent same-series dispersion.
